subject: SIG: clarification — prompt/log retention, training on customer data (Karuna Health)
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Megan O'Leary <moleary@karuna.health>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG answers + summary — prompt logs, retention, training

Hi Megan,

Attached is our completed SIG extract focused on data handling and training questions (redwood_SIG_answers_v2.pdf). Below are the short answers pulled from the document for your procurement/security review — happy to expand where useful: 

- Prompt + response logs: Default hosted retention window is 14 days (configurable). Dedicated and Private deployments can be contractually set to 0-day retention for logs.
- Purpose of logs: debugging, abuse detection, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring.
- Training on customer data: Redwood does NOT train models on customer data by default. Training or model fine-tuning on customer inputs occurs only with explicit, written customer opt-in and a separate agreement.
- Access: Logs are accessible only to authorized roles (SRE, Support, Security) and all access is logged in immutable audit trails.
- Encryption: Data encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (KMS-managed keys).

I also attached a retention_matrix.xlsx that maps default TTLs by product tier and deployment mode — that should help procurement pick the right option.

Next steps: let me know if you want a one-page statement we can paste into the contract, or we can tighten the language for your security team.

Thanks —
Chloe Martin
Security & Compliance Liaison
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_SIG_answers_v2.pdf, retention_matrix.xlsx
From: Megan O'Leary <moleary@karuna.health>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG answers + summary — prompt logs, retention, training

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the doc and the matrix — very helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our InfoSec and procurement teams before we move this to legal: 

1) When you say "Default hosted retention window is 14 days", can you confirm whether that includes any intermediate caching (KV/prefix caches) or is strictly request/response logs? We need to know if any customer inputs are persisted beyond immediate request completion.
2) On training: we need a sentence that we can include in our DPA stating that customer inputs will not be used to improve model weights without explicit opt-in. Would you provide a signed statement or suggest contract language?
3) Who can view the logs? Your note mentions roles — do humans ever review raw prompts verbatim for debugging? If so, are the prompts redacted/anonymized?

Finally, procurement asked if you can provide a short evidence bundle (S3 path or drive) with screenshots of the retention config page and an export of an audit log showing access events. If you have a DPA/DocuSign link we can pre-fill, that speeds things up.

Megan O'Leary
Head of Security Operations
Karuna Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG answers + summary — prompt logs, retention, training

Chloe — drafting a concise reply for Megan. Pulling in Priyom for procurement language and Neha for engineering details (KV cache and audit log example). Proposed bullets to send: 

- "Hosted prompt/response logs are retained for 14 days by default. This does not include ephemeral KV cache entries used for active session acceleration; KV cache entries are kept in-memory and persisted to disk only transiently and are cleared after session completion. Customers can request a shorter TTL or 0-day retention in Dedicated/Private deployments via contract."
- "Redwood does not use customer inputs to update model weights, train, or fine-tune models unless there is an explicit written opt-in. We can include the following clause in the DPA: 'Provider will not use Customer Data as training data to update model weights or internal datasets without the Customer’s prior written consent.'"
- "Authorized human review: Support and SRE may view raw logs for debugging, but access is restricted and subject to role-based access control and audited — examples of audit records will be provided."

If that looks good I'll send it, attaching the retention matrix and a sanitized audit log sample.

-Marcus

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Megan O'Leary <moleary@karuna.health>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG answers + summary — prompt logs, retention, training

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear list. See inline answers below and a short contract-ready sentence you can paste into the DPA. I've attached the evidence bundle to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/karuna/sig/evidence (attachment: redwood_SIG_answers_v2.pdf, retention_matrix.xlsx).

1) Caches vs logs:
- Prompt/response logs: default retention = 14 days for Redwood-hosted API.
- KV/prefix cache: primarily in-memory with minimal, encrypted on-disk persistence for efficient recovery; these artifacts are ephemeral and are cleared on session termination. We consider KV cache entries transient and not part of long-term retention.

2) Contract language (suggested DPA clause):
- "Provider will not use Customer Data (including prompts and generation outputs) to train, fine-tune, or improve Provider models or datasets without the Customer’s prior written consent.
- Provider may process Customer Data for operational purposes (e.g., debugging, abuse detection, billing) in accordance with this DPA and will maintain role-based, auditable controls on access."

3) Human access and redaction:
- Authorized personnel in Support, SRE, and Security may access raw logs for troubleshooting and incident response. Access requires justification, is granted via RBAC, and every access generates an audit record that is retained per our audit retention policy. We can provide a sanitized sample audit log showing access events and the fields captured (user, role, timestamp, reason).

Evidence we are sending now (Drive link and attached PDF/Excel):
- redwood_SIG_answers_v2.pdf (completed SIG extract + references to SOC2 and encryption controls)
- retention_matrix.xlsx (TTL defaults by deployment and options for contractual exceptions)
- sanitized_audit_log_sample.csv (available in Drive folder)

Notes on deployment options:
- Hosted: default 14-day prompt/response retention; near-term cache transient.
- Dedicated: retention configurable via admin console; can be set to 0 days (no persisted logs) under reserved capacity contract.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer controls all retention via local config — Redwood supports a 0-day retention setup.

If procurement wants a single-line signed statement, happy to have Legal sign the clause above and return as a PDF or DocuSign envelope. Let me know what tone they prefer.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Security & Compliance Liaison
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_SIG_answers_v2.pdf, retention_matrix.xlsx

Chloe — this is perfect, thank you. Can you have Legal produce a short PDF with the clause and signatory block? If you can send via DocuSign that would be ideal — I'll attach the redlined DPA we plan to send back once we receive your statement.

I'll also review the sanitized audit log sample in the Drive link this afternoon. If everything checks out, we can move to signatures next week.

Thanks again —
Megan
